affiliations.organization_name_as_found: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
affiliations.date_precision: The 1948 Congressional Record gives the exact Board start date; Harvard independently describes his 1944 acceptance of a European economic analyst position. Neither source states the dates or administrative relationship of his OSS service.
affiliations.research_notes: Published as a documented pre-OSS government affiliation, not as the proven immediate predecessor. The physical personnel file is needed to establish whether the Board appointment continued during OSS service, involved a detail, or was interrupted.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Alexander Gerschenkron is the economist documented at the Federal Reserve Board beginning in 1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name in the OSS index matches the official federal personnel statement and Harvard archival biography in name, profession, degree and Washington career.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from a distinctive exact name plus consistent official and institutional biographical identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Board appointment is precisely dated; the OSS service dates and administrative relationship remain unestablished.
claims.match_notes: No rank or private identifier appears in the index, so identity is not labeled confirmed until the Box 269 file is compared.

claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the distinctive exact name and consistent profession, degree and Washington chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented wartime affiliation beginning before the 1945 end of OSS, but not proven to be the immediate predecessor to OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The Board is modeled as a government assignment, not a private employer. The public profile explicitly preserves the unresolved OSS transition.
